title: Rules document
description: The rules layer of a pack: fields and their formulas, content types, game settings, situational choices, result bands, shared actions, always-on effects, character-level choices, constraints and display hints. A pack may split its rules over several files in `rules/`; every section is optional and the build merges them. IDs must be unique across the merged result.

families.description: Named lists of keys: any mapping key of the pack's rules documents that holds `{<name>}` stands for one entry per value, with `{<name>}` replaced in the key and in every string of the entry. Declared once per pack, in any rules document; seen by the pack and the packs that depend on it. A qualified name (`<pack>:<name>`) adds values to that pack's family. Expanded by the engine with the packs loaded together; a built release keeps it as written.

extendEnums.description: Values this pack adds to a dependency's open enums (`open: true`), by the enum's address, its text key root qualified with its pack: `<pack>:fields.<field>` (a rules field), `<pack>:types.<type>.fields.<field>` (an item field), `<pack>:types.<type>.state.<key>` (a state key), `<pack>:actions.<action>.params.<param>` (a rules action's parameter), `<pack>:<item>.state.<key>` (an item's own state key) or `<pack>:<item>.actions.<action>.params.<param>` (an item's inline action's parameter). Each value is named in this pack's text under the key the enum's own pack would use (`types.weapon.fields.damageType.values.sonic.name`). Added after the enum's own values, in load order, each once (rules-and-fields.md, "Open enums").

extendChoices.description: Options this pack adds to a dependency's choices, without overriding the item: by owner, `<pack>:<content id>` or `<pack>:rules` (a rules-level choice), then by choice ID (`<choice>/<option>/<choice>` for a choice of an inline option; a slotted choice's declared ID, for every slot). An addition is the choice's own kind: `items` for an items choice, `values` for written values, `options` (inline options) for inline options. The added options come after the choice's own, then each loaded pack's in load order; a repeated item or value is offered once, an inline option ID that's there already is `duplicate-id`. Added inline options read this pack's fields, and are named in this pack's text under the key the owner's pack would use (`<owner>.choices.<choice>.options.<id>.name`). Applied after every override (content.md, "Adding options to a dependency's choices").

viewFields.description: Named sets of declared fields read from other characters: a link slot's or a participant role's `fields` may name one instead of declaring them again. Expanded before the pack loads.

links.description: Link slots: named places for another character, such as a scoundrel's crew. A character file saves which character fills each slot (`links`), and the app passes that character's view (`{ id, values }`) to the calls. Formulas read it as `links.<slot>`. Slot IDs are names, qualified like field IDs. Text: `links.<slot>.name` (optional).

templateFields.description: Item fields every template may set, by name, merged across packs: a name declared again must have the same `type` (and `of` and `values`), else the load error `template-field-mismatch`; the later declaration replaces the earlier. A copy's `item` has each one its content type doesn't declare: the last value its templates give, else the declaration's `default`, else it is absent. Each is named by `templateFields.<name>.name` (required) and `.description` (optional) in the declaring pack's text.

rollTallies.description: Roll tallies: named integer counters on a roll that effects add to without changing its total. Roll steps expose them as `steps.<id>.tallies.<name>`, result bands as `roll.tallies.<name>`. Text: `tallies.<name>.name` (optional).

resultBands.description: Named sets of result bands, e.g. FitD's 1–3 / 4–5 / 6 / critical. Bands are checked in order; the first whose `when` is true wins. Formulas see the roll as `roll` (`roll.total`, `roll.faces`, `roll.kept`) and the running action's `flags`, `params` and `steps` (provisional). A set is a list of bands, or `{ value, bands }`: `value` is evaluated once per classification, before the bands, which read it as `roll.value`.

value.description: A formula in the band context, evaluated once each time the set classifies a roll; its bands read it as `roll.value`, and the roll step's result keeps it as `bandValue`.

actions.description: Shared actions items and content types can `use`. A shared action has no `scope`: the `use` that lists it does.

effects.description: Effects that are always active (critical hits doubling damage dice).

followUps.description: What the rules say should happen next when a change does something to the character: listed by applyChanges, never run by it.

creation.description: How a character is created: the starting points an app offers for a new character, each running a rules action. An app offers a guided run of every start, a random run of a start with `random`, and always a blank sheet (manual creation). A start's text is `creation.<id>.name`. Packs' lists are concatenated in load order, and a later start with the same `id` replaces the earlier one in its place. Without any start, characters are created by hand only.

standardCopies.description: Content every character of the game holds a copy of, e.g. FitD's standard gear: queries that read only `item`, resolved by loadRuleset. Each match is a standard copy with the instance ID `<pack>-<local ID>`, the colon and dots as hyphens, in `inventory` for carried types and `features` otherwise; the character file saves it only once it differs from its defaults.

immuneTo.description: Applied content every character of the game can't be affected by while the immunity's `when` holds, e.g. a monster's condition immunities listed in an input set field. Without `scope`: the rules are always a holder.

constraints.description: Game rules checked against the current character. A failing check is a rules issue with code `constraint-failed` and this constraint's ID. With `copies`, the check runs once per copy of a content type, and each copy that fails is an issue of its own.

data.description: Values reported with the issue so the app can render it (`limit: 3`).

copies.description: Check each of the character's copies of this content type (`features` and `inventory`, standard copies included) whose `where` holds, with `item` and `self` that copy's item and copy, as a choice step over copies sees them (its computed values included). Each failing copy is its own `constraint-failed`, its instance ID in `data.entry` and its own `data` values evaluated for it.

tags.description: The tags this pack declares. Every tag the pack uses (content, fields, rolls, effects, changes, `tag` set members) must be declared here or by a dependency. Declaring `damage.fire` also declares `damage`. Optional text: `tags.<tag>.name`.

bandList.description: Result bands, checked in order. At most one band is the set's `success` threshold.

success.description: This band is the roll's success threshold: what an app shows as what the roll needs ("what you need"). A set without one has no threshold to show (a ladder, a table).

rounding.description: How the game rounds results of multiply effects and decimal division (5E rounds down). Default `floor`.

default.description: Policy for effects sharing a stack key that has no specific policy. Default `addAll`.

roundIncoming.description: How multiply effects on incoming changes round: `value` rounds the signed amount (default); `magnitude` rounds its size and restores the sign, so halving −11 damage gives −5 with `floor` (5E: round down the damage).

rollModifiers.description: How opposing roll modifiers combine. `advantage`: `cancel` (default; advantage and disadvantage together cancel, and any number of sources give one extra die), `net` (the difference between the counts of sources decides the direction and number of extra dice), or `stack` (every source adds a die; both kinds together is an error in the pack).

pack.description: The pack the linked character is expected to use. Optional, and not a dependency: any character whose view has the declared fields may fill the slot. When this pack is loaded alongside, loadRuleset and the build check each declared field against it (`link-field-mismatch`); the engine never checks the linked character's packs.

fields.description: The fields this pack reads from the linked character, typed, so formulas type-check without the other pack; or the name of a `viewFields` set.

creationStart.description: One way to start creating a character: a rules action, run on a character with `creating: true`.

id.description: The start's ID, unique across the loaded packs (a later pack's start with the same ID replaces it). Text: `creation.<id>.name` and, optionally, `creation.<id>.description`.

action.description: A rules action: a local or qualified action ID. Every parameter it requires must be given in `params`.

params.description: Parameters the start passes to the action, as literal values, so two starts can share one action.

random.description: Default false. Set it only when the source creates characters at random: running the action with every checkpoint automatic (`{ dice: auto, choices: auto, allocations: auto }`) makes a character the source's own random creation could produce. Without it, an automatic run takes each step's recommendation, a default character rather than a random one. `pnpm validate` warns about a step that would pause in such a run: a choice step over a written list, or an `allocate` step, without `recommend`.
